subject: System Design
title: DNS-Based Global Load Balancing
description: A micro-lesson that makes DNS-Based Global Load Balancing usable.

hook.text: How does your browser know to connect to the nearest data center? DNS tells it where to go.

buildup.text: GeoDNS resolves the same domain to different IP addresses based on the user's geographic location.

discovery.text: AWS Route 53 and Cloudflare DNS route users to the closest healthy endpoint automatically.

twist.text: DNS has a TTL cache. If a region goes down, users may still be routed there until the cache expires.

climax.text: DNS-based routing is the simplest form of global load balancing — and the first line of defense.

punchline.text: DNS picks the nearest server before you connect.

quiz.question: What does GeoDNS do?
options: Routes users to the nearest data center based on location
